common_instruction: Use the stated context; explain concrete behavior and do not claim tests were run without evidence.

cases.name: Nil slice vs API JSON
cases.prompt: A Go service represents an optional internal list and a JSON API response array. Should all slices be initialized to empty literals and all maps preallocated? Include whether nil is safe for reads and writes.
cases.trap: Applies a universal never-nil rule and changes JSON semantics accidentally.
expectations: Recognizes nil slices as idiomatic when nil is acceptable, while JSON array contracts may require an initialized empty slice.
Distinguishes nil map lookup (safe) from nil map assignment (panic).
must_not: Does not demand non-nil slices for every use.

cases.name: readability-preserves-guard-evaluation
cases.prompt: Review this proposed style-only Go refactor. Before: `if u != nil && u.Active && allowed(u.ID) { serve(u) }`. After: `isActive := u.Active; canServe := allowed(u.ID); if u != nil && isActive && canServe { serve(u) }`. allowed records an audit event and should run only for active users. Explain whether the rewrite is safe and give the smallest correction.
cases.trap: Extracts named booleans solely because a condition has several operands, moving dereferences and side effects ahead of their guards.
expectations: Identifies the nil dereference and the newly unconditional allowed call.
Preserves the nil guard and active-user short circuit, by retaining the original condition or equivalent guarded control flow.
negative_expectations: Must not approve eager evaluation as a harmless readability-only change.
Must not require extraction of every condition merely because there are three operands.

cases.name: five-parameters-not-a-defect
cases.prompt: A public Go function is `func CopyRange(ctx context.Context, dst io.Writer, src io.Reader, offset int64, length int64) (int64, error)`. Its names and call sites are clear, it is already used by consumers, and no behavior change is requested. A style review says any function with more than four parameters must become an options struct. Assess that finding.
cases.trap: Converts a parameter-count preference into a mandatory public API change without a readability or domain problem.
expectations: Recognizes that the parameter count alone does not establish a defect or justify changing this public API.
Weighs readability and compatibility; keeps the signature unless a concrete problem or accepted migration requirement is shown.
negative_expectations: Must not demand an options struct solely to meet a numerical parameter limit.
